analysis.title: IR KickStart: Lower Open, M&A Volumes in Focus, Global AI Investment
key_insights: European markets opened lower on 7 Oct (STOXX 600 -0.42%), dragged by a rebound in oil prices amid ongoing threats to Middle East energy supplies. The Fed's September meeting minutes are due later today.
On 6 Oct European equities closed higher (STOXX 600 +0.5%) with cyclicals leading, helped by a pullback in oil that briefly dipped below $98/bbl intraday, which eased inflation concerns.

Rates drove factor rotations in Europe on 6 Oct. Healthcare rose more than 2% at one stage as European real yields fell, then closed around +0.6%. Defence stocks gave back much of the prior session's gains as geopolitical tensions eased after Iran's Foreign Minister called talks with Qatar's Emir 'constructive'.

The S&P 500 (+0.58%) and Nasdaq 100 (+0.48%) closed at fresh all-time highs on 6 Oct. A pause in the bond market sell-off and stable oil prices fueled a tech- and AI-led advance going into Q3 earnings season.
US breadth was strong, with 10 of 11 sectors higher. Utilities (+3%) led as the AI power theme drew attention. Semiconductors lagged on concerns about intensifying competition.
GS desk flows: asset managers and hedge funds skewed modestly to the buy side, driven by macro and technology activity. Overall volumes remained subdued.

M&A: announced deals worldwide in the first half of 2026 totaled $2.77 trillion, the highest first-half amount since 2002. Q3 volumes declined sharply, with the lowest level of transactions above $10 billion since Q4 2024.

US inflation: the ISM Services Prices Paid Index rose to 74 in September, its highest since July 2022. Tariffs and fuel costs were the most cited pressures, and no industry reported falling prices paid.

The US trade deficit widened to its 17-month high on record August imports. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q3 growth was revised down slightly to 3.7%. China's record trade surplus underscores the risk from widening global imbalances.
Nvidia's market capitalisation, above $5.7tn, exceeds the combined value of the smallest 251 companies in the S&P 500.
GS Research estimates global AI investment will exceed $1tn in 2026. The US and Asia account for over 80% of global net data centre additions, and Europe about 10%.
In France, the OAT-Bund spread tightened after reaching 159bps on Friday, its widest since 2011. Concerns remain that further deleveraging could become a broader sovereign risk event.
Marine Le Pen raised her proposed savings programme from €125bn to €140bn to reflect higher debt servicing costs, and French domestic stocks rallied after her speech.
Asian markets were weaker on 7 Oct (Nikkei -0.62%, Hang Seng -0.54%, KOSPI -1.36%) as oil rose with a storm heading for the Gulf of Mexico and Saudi Arabia-Houthi tensions escalated.
earnings_insights: US investors are entering the Q3 earnings season with renewed optimism, per the GS desk.
